verdict.rationale: MIT-licensed open-source headless coding agent adopted as the Build Studio 'opencode' dispatch engine. It runs inside the existing sandbox against the install's OWN local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so it introduces no vendor credential and no network egress beyond the operator's own model server. Install mechanism, runtime, and dispatch flags were verified live on node:24-alpine (musl). Conditional pending the formal EP-GOVERN-002 multi-agent evaluation to upgrade to 'approved'.

conditions: sandbox-only — runs inside the Build Studio sandbox container, never on the host or portal
local-endpoint-only — pointed at the install's local OpenAI-compatible endpoint; no external provider config
no credential injected — local servers need none; the opencode.json apiKey is a dummy
capability tier stays 'preview' until Phase 3 eval evidence on a real local model

findings.title: License: MIT
findings.description: OpenCode is MIT-licensed (OSI-approved), compatible with the platform. Rejected alternative Crush is FSL-1.1 (not OSI) for this reason.

findings.title: npm postinstall does not detect musl (upstream #9571)
findings.description: The opencode-ai npm postinstall constructs the glibc binary name and never tries the -musl variant, so `npm install -g opencode-ai` fails/links the wrong binary on the Alpine sandbox base.
findings.recommendation: Bypass npm: fetch the pinned opencode-linux-x64-baseline-musl release tarball directly into the image (the grok pattern). Implemented in Dockerfile.sandbox.
findings.mitigation: Direct tarball install + `opencode --version` build gate as root and the node user.

findings.title: Install + dispatch contract verified live on node:24-alpine
findings.description: Probe build confirmed: baseline-musl tarball runs as root and the node user (uid 1000) printing version 1.17.4 exit 0 with only libstdc++/libgcc (no gcompat); the dispatch flags --dir, -m provider/model, --format json, --dangerously-skip-permissions all exist on this pinned version; the @ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider pre-seeds into ~/.cache/opencode/packages/... for air-gapped first run.
findings.recommendation: Proceed. Full happy-path (opencode run against a real local model) is the Phase 3 functional gate.

verdict.rationale: Standards-based self-hosted X.509 CA selected by governed decision DI-236363AB3AA3. The pinned image passed an isolated health/fingerprint/rollback smoke test. Adoption is limited to organization HTTPS leaf issuance under the documented network, secret-custody, provisioner, and advisory-monitoring conditions.

conditions: do not enable SCEP; review ACME separately before enabling it
store the CA password in a file-backed secret and keys in the dedicated PKI volume
bind the CA only to an explicitly selected private address or private overlay network
retain federation candidate validation, dual approval, projection review, and revocation independently of PKI

findings.title: Recent critical provisioner advisories are patched in the approved version
findings.description: CVE-2025-44005 affected ACME/SCEP through 0.28.4 and CVE-2026-30836 affected SCEP before 0.30.0. The approved 0.30.2 image contains both fixes; DPF does not enable SCEP.
findings.recommendation: Pin the evaluated digest and re-evaluate on every security advisory or version bump.
findings.mitigation: Digest pin, unused-provisioner disablement, private network binding, advisory monitoring.

findings.title: Apache-2.0 and self-hosted data path
findings.description: Step CA is Apache-2.0 licensed and the selected deployment sends no certificate or key data to Smallstep-hosted services.

findings.title: Pinned image health and rollback verified
findings.description: The evaluated image started with a disposable volume on a loopback-only random port, returned ok from step ca health, produced a SHA-256 root fingerprint, and was removed with its volume.
findings.evidence: Local isolated Docker integration test, 2026-07-20; digest sha256:a2b17872915c193259b75a5474c398326f41bd199f0842093e52cf4182bc8270
